Financial Aid Information.Description: Provides financial assistance to eligible South African students and permanent residents from low-income households (gross household income not exceeding R350,000 per annum for students without disabilities, or R600,000 for students with disabilities). Funding covers tuition fees, registration fees, prescribed textbooks, accommodation (capped at university residence rates or private accommodation up to the same limit), transport allowances (for non-residents), living allowances, and personal care allowances (for students in catered residences).

Application.Period: Typically open on 2025-09-01 and close on 2025-11-30
Requirements: Proof of acceptance or provisional acceptance at UJ for first-year students.
Certified copies of ID, parents’/guardians’ IDs, proof of income (payslips, affidavits if unemployed, or SASSA grant proof), and academic records.
Students must reapply annually and meet academic progression requirements.
Application.Note: NSFAS does not fund postgraduate qualifications (e.g., Honours, Master’s, or PhD) as of 2021; explore options like the National Research Foundation (NRF).

Financial Aid Information.Description: Awarded to academically outstanding students based on final Grade 12 results or prior academic performance at UJ. Available for undergraduate students pursuing a degree or formal diploma, automatically evaluated for qualifying registered students.
Eligibility: First-year students: APS of 37 or higher and at least 70% in six best subjects (excluding Life Orientation).
Returning students: Overall average of 75% or higher in the previous academic year.
Covers up to 100% of tuition fees, varying by faculty and academic performance.
Orange Carpet Rewards Programme offers additional benefits for top-performing matriculants (APS ≥ 37 and 70%+ in six best subjects), including stipends or book allowances.
Financial Aid Information.Note: Students receiving NSFAS funding may not receive additional UJ merit bursaries to avoid overfunding, but the award is recorded on their transcript.

Financial Aid Information.Description: Offered by UJ’s nine faculties, particularly for Honours, Master’s, and Doctoral programs, based on academic merit, financial need, or specific criteria (e.g., research focus or leadership qualities).

Faculty of Science Honours Bursary.Coverage: Full tuition fees for students accepted into an Honours program, subject to availability of funds.

Examples.Faculty of Science Master’s and Doctoral: Funding for postgraduate research, with varying amounts based on budget and project requirements.

College of Business and Economics Bursar.Programs: BCom Honours in Financial Planning or MCom in Quantitative Finance

Financial Aid Information.Application: Submit faculty-specific forms (available on the UJ website or from faculty offices) with additional documents like CV, motivation letter, or research proposal.

Financial Aid Information.Description: Facilitated by UJ, offered by private companies, municipalities, government departments, and other organizations based on academic merit, financial need, or specific criteria like geographic location or field of study.
Examples: Bursaries for specific fields: Engineering, IT, or Health Sciences (e.g., Johannesburg City Power Bursaries for Undergraduate Studies 2025).
Government-funded bursaries: Funza Lushaka for Education students or Department of Labour bursaries for students with disabilities.
Financial Aid Information.Application: Apply directly to the sponsoring organization, adhering to their deadlines and requirements. Supporting documents include certified ID copies, academic records, and proof of financial need.
Financial Aid Information.Note: UJ limits multiple awards to ensure equitable distribution of funds. Avoid scams promising bursaries for a fee and report suspicious activities to uj@thehotline.co.za.

Financial Aid Information.Description: Provides financial assistance to financially needy and academically deserving students. Students with no historical debt are automatically unblocked for registration upon approval. Those with outstanding debt must follow the Acknowledgement of Debt (AOD) process.
Financial Aid Information.Application: Submit online via the UJ Student Life and Governance portal (https://apps.uj.ac.za/StudentLifeAndGovernance).
Financial Aid Information.Note: Specific application dates for 2026 will be announced on the UJ website, typically aligning with the academic year.

Financial Aid Information.Description: UJ offers work-study opportunities for students to earn income while studying, including on-campus roles like tutoring, library assistance, or administrative support. External internship programs provide additional funding and professional experience.
Financial Aid Information.Eligibility: Available to undergraduate and postgraduate students; must balance work hours with academic requirements.
Financial Aid Information.Application: Details and application processes available through the UJ Student Finance office or faculty coordinators.

Financial Aid Information.Description: UJ partners with Eduloan (now Fundi) to provide study loans for students who do not qualify for NSFAS or bursaries, covering tuition, accommodation, and study materials with flexible repayment options. Other private financial institutions may also offer student loans.
Financial Aid Information.Application: Apply directly through the provider (e.g., https://www.fundi.co.za). Supporting documents include proof of registration, ID, and financial details of the applicant or sponsor.
Financial Aid Information.Note: Students with outstanding debt from prior years must follow the Acknowledgement of Debt (AOD) process before registering.

Accommodation Information.Description: Residence applications for the 2026 academic year open on 2025-04-01 and close on 2025-09-30, aligning with the undergraduate and postgraduate academic application period. On-campus accommodation is available at UJ’s four campuses: Auckland Park Kingsway (APK), Auckland Park Bunting Road (APB), Doornfontein (DFC), and Soweto (SWC).
Accommodation Information.Application: Apply simultaneously with academic application via the UJ online application portal (https://www.uj.ac.za/admissions-aid/accommodation/).
Accommodation Information.Deposit: R1,220 (non-refundable, subject to change; confirm 2026 rates in November 2025).
Accommodation Information.Note: Spaces are limited, and allocation is based on academic merit, financial need, and application date. First-year students are prioritized. Applicants must upload certified copies of their ID, academic records, and proof of academic application. Successful applicants receive confirmation via the UJ student portal (https://student.uj.ac.za/status.aspx). Late applications may be considered subject to availability.
Accommodation Information.Disability Support: Contact the Disability Unit at disabilityunit@uj.ac.za or +27 (0)11 559 3745 for disability-friendly accommodation (e.g., wheelchair-accessible rooms).

Accommodation Information.Description: Each UJ campus has dedicated residence managers to assist with accommodation queries and student support.
Accommodation Information.Note: Residence managers handle room allocations, maintenance requests, and student welfare.

Accommodation Information.Description: UJ-accredited off-campus residences within a 2 km radius of UJ’s campuses (APK, APB, DFC, SWC), vetted for safety, security, and quality standards, including amenities like electricity, water, Wi-Fi, study areas, and transport services.
Accommodation Information.Application: Apply directly to accredited POSA providers listed on the UJ website (https://www.uj.ac.za/admissions-aid/accommodation/posa-accredited-list/).
Accommodation Information.Note: Costs vary depending on provider and amenities. NSFAS-funded students can use their accommodation allowance for POSA, capped at UJ residence rates. Verify accreditation to avoid scams and report suspicious providers to uj@thehotline.co.za. International students must ensure POSA providers comply with visa accommodation requirements.

Accommodation Information.Description: On-campus residence fees for 2026 will be confirmed in November 2025 and typically increase by 5–10% annually. For 2025, average residence fees range from R39,000 to R60,000 per year, depending on the campus and room type (single, double, or self-catering).
Accommodation Information.Deposit: R1,220 (non-refundable, payable via bank transfer or at the UJ Cash Office).
Accommodation Information.Note: NSFAS-funded students have residence fees covered up to the university’s capped rate. Students with outstanding residence fees from previous years must complete an Acknowledgement of Debt (AOD) process to register. International students must provide proof of medical aid cover and comply with South African immigration regulations.

Accommodation Information.Description: UJ residences offer furnished rooms (bed, desk, wardrobe), Wi-Fi, study areas, communal kitchens (in self-catering units), laundry facilities, 24/7 security, and access control. Some residences provide catering services (e.g., dining halls with meal plans).

Campus Offerings.APK: Largest campus with multiple residences (e.g., Impumelelo, Goudstad), offering single and double rooms, some with en-suite bathrooms.

Campus Offerings.APB: Smaller residences like Sophiatown, ideal for quieter environments.

Campus Offerings.DFC: Modern facilities like Habitat and Kilimanjaro, suited for Engineering and Health Sciences students.

Campus Offerings.SWC: Compact residences like YWCA, fostering a close-knit community.

Accommodation Information.Note: Residences include recreational areas (e.g., TV rooms, sports facilities) and access to UJ’s academic support services (e.g., libraries, tutoring). Residence life programs promote community engagement through events and leadership opportunities.

Accommodation Information.Description: International students can apply for on-campus residences or accredited POSA, subject to the same deadlines and processes as local students (2025-04-01 to 2025-09-30). On-campus accommodation is recommended for ease of integration.
Requirements: Valid study visa and proof of medical aid cover (recognized in South Africa).
International levy: Approximately R2,000 for SADC and African countries (subject to change; confirm 2026 rates in November 2025).
Accommodation Information.Note: The Division for Internationalisation assists with accommodation queries and visa compliance. Students choosing POSA must ensure the provider meets visa requirements (e.g., proof of address for Home Affairs). Early application is advised due to limited spaces and visa processing times (3–6 months).
